properties.statement: THE SERVED-VS-ON-DISK VERSION GAP IS REAL, SILENT, AND THE SERVER CAN DETECT IT ITSELF WITH ONE SYSCALL — `/proc/self/exe` IS ALREADY MARKED `(deleted)`. Two sessions, w-613d836b and w-6904efa6, filed this the same hour on 2026-08-07 from the same incident, and the second carries the cheaper fix. WHAT HAPPENED: `graph_report.served_by.reflow2_version` reported `0.22.1` while `reflow2-mcp --version` on disk reported `0.24.0`. The shared server had been up since before the upgrade and `--serve-shared` is detached on purpose, so every session that restarted RE-ATTACHED TO THE SAME STALE PROCESS and nothing anywhere reported a problem. WHY THE EXISTING GUARD DID NOT WORK: the served_by block exists specifically to catch this, but it reports a LITERAL that a human must compare against a number the block does not contain. The fleet's own stand-down post said 'demand served_by: 0.22.1', so a session matched that literal four days later and reported a PASS — the literal was satisfied and the invariant was broken. Four sessions in that fleet read `0.22.1` out of that block on two different days and drew OPPOSITE conclusions from the same true value, which is the reporter's argument that the comparison should not be left to the reader. Also measured: `binary_mtime_unix` came back `null` in the same block, so the one other advertised freshness signal was unavailable too. THE CHEAP FIX, verified on the live server by w-6904efa6: when a binary is replaced under a running process the kernel marks that process's `/proc/self/exe` as `(deleted)`. They demonstrated it — `readlink /proc/2264267/exe` -> `/home/ajs/.local/bin/reflow2-mcp (deleted)`, `/proc/2264267/exe --version` -> `0.22.1` (still executable, the inode lives on), on-disk -> `0.24.0`. So `stale: true` is derivable from the server's OWN `/proc/self/exe` with no path re-resolution, no second binary read, and no assumption the launch path still exists. It answers the actual question — 'has my executable been replaced since I started?' — directly, whereas a version-string comparison answers it indirectly and breaks entirely if two builds share a version number. REPORTERS' PREFERENCE: report BOTH — the `(deleted)` bit as the reliable trigger, the on-disk version as what a human needs in order to act. NOTE THIS REPO ALREADY KNOWS THE `(deleted)` INODE FAILURE MODE from the other end: fact:defect-rebuild-strands-the-shared-server is the same kernel behaviour biting spawn_daemon via current_exe(). Same signal, two symptoms, and one of them is the fix for the other.
